newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Fiery Belarus leader says he is sick of critics.
newsitem.headline: Fiery Belarus leader says he is sick of critics.

text.p: Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko on Wednesday hit out at opponents who have accused him of building a dictatorship in the former Soviet republic, saying they were spreading lies about him.
Lukashenko, who won a landslide victory two years ago on a platform of fighting corruption and re-building ties with Moscow, also said he was sick of the West criticising him.
The 41-year-old leader was in Moscow on Wednesday to meet President Boris Yeltsin and discuss integration with Russia.
Addressing a news conference, he said he wanted to clear up "disinformation" being spread by Belarussian journalists who he said all supported the opposition.
Lukashenko stands accused of acting undemocratically by calling an "All-Belarus" congress to discuss constitutional changes on Saturday, apparently in a bid to bypass parliament.
He has called a referendum for November 7 on a new constitution which will give him another unelected five years in power and broaden his authority.
But a majority of parliamentary deputies have united against him and called for a referendum on November 24 to abolish the post of president altogether.
Earlier in Minsk, the visiting head of the Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly said only parliament had the right to fix the referendum's date.
Leni Fischer warned Lukashenko that his plans to increase his own powers might divide the former Soviet republic.
Parliamentary speaker Semyon Sharetsky told Fischer that violence might break out during pro- and anti-Lukashenko gatherings over the referendum this weekend.
Up to 200 people were given short jail terms after mass rallies against Lukashenko's policies in April this year led to clashes with police.
But Lukashenko said it was parliament which was destroying the country because it was split between anti-reform communists and liberals who he called "national radicals".
He also hit out at Western criticism, saying: "You know, Belarus has already had enough of these protests."

The leading commentator on Belarus state television, which is controlled by Lukashenko, said on Tuesday that the ambassadors of Britain, Italy, Germany and France had issued a joint protest about Lukashenko's behaviour on Monday.
A spokeswoman for the British embassy confirmed a group of ambassadors had launched an initiative on Monday but gave few details and declined to comment on the protest.
Lukashenko accused them of inappropriate behaviour for saying his congress was anti-constitutional and saying they would refuse to recognise the results of his referendum.
"Since we are an independent and sovereign state, we will naturally not permit...foreign representatives to behave, let us say, worse than at home," he added.
